1. The animation shows the trade-off between paying extra on a mortgage and using that money some other way. Paying extra on the loan counts as a guaranteed return equal to the mortgage rate. At the Oct 8, 2026 survey rate that is 7.40% a year, before taxes. That figure is the "bar" any other use of the money would have to beat.

2. A character named Tessa stands next to her house, holding a dollar bill. The bill moves up onto a gray bar. The bar then gets a scale marked "zero" at the bottom and "7.40%" at the top, and the label "the bar: 7.40% a year, before taxes" appears. The label "interest no longer charged" appears under the bill on the bar. Last, a dashed, faded bill labeled "any other use" appears beside the bar, followed by the words "not tested".

3. Putting a dollar toward the mortgage earns 7.40% a year by removing interest you would otherwise pay. Any other use of that dollar, such as investing it, would have to do better than 7.40% to come out ahead. The animation does not say whether any other use would clear that bar, which is what "not tested" means. The captions "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "US only · history, not a forecast" mark it as a generic example, not a prediction.

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer could take away a way of comparing the two options: measure investing against the 7.40% the mortgage pays. It does not say which choice is better.

5. The comparison to a 7.40% bar came from the animation's picture and text. Nothing in it told the viewer to pay extra or to invest. I have added no advice of my own.
